update.title: Built a desktop service manager with live logs
update.summary: Built a GTK dashboard for opted-in systemd user services, with cached live status, lifecycle controls, and a filterable shared journal stream.

preview.description: Process Manager with a selected service, enabled lifecycle controls, and a populated live journal view.

blocks.body:
## Operate background services from one place

I built Process Manager because the desktop depended on a growing set of systemd user services, but checking and controlling them required repeated terminal commands. The GTK dashboard discovers opted-in services and provides explicit start, stop, restart, enable, and disable actions while systemd retains responsibility for process lifetime and restart policy.

## Keep repeated status checks lightweight

The grouped service list shows state, port, uptime, and memory use with distinct running, failed, stopped, starting, and stopping states. A two-second cache gathers each service status once per refresh window instead of repeating several subprocess calls every second. Lifecycle actions invalidate the affected entry so the UI can reconcile immediately.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  Discovery[Opt-in service discovery] --> Cache[Two-second status cache]
  Systemd[systemd user manager] --> Cache
  Cache --> List[Grouped service list]
  List --> Selection[Selected service context]
  Selection --> Actions[Start, stop, restart, enable]
  Journal[journalctl JSON stream] --> Buffer[Bounded parsed log buffer]
  Buffer --> Filters[Service, level, and text filters]
  Filters --> Selection
blocks.description: Status, controls, and live logs converge on the same selected systemd unit while systemd retains process ownership.

blocks.body:
## Make live logs part of the workspace

One background `journalctl --user -f -o json` stream loads recent entries and follows every watched unit. Parsed priority levels feed a bounded buffer through a GTK-safe queue. The interface can isolate one service or combine them, filter severity, search text, clear the view, and pause auto-scroll while an earlier failure is inspected.
